neighbours.label: size/quantity adjective in a noun phrase about physical scale or amount ('a large number of', 'a relatively big size', 'little to no')
fire: The ancient wall was decorated with a large number of carved figures.
Engineers built the tank to a fairly big size so it could hold rainwater.
These old batteries hold little to no charge after a cold night.
The farm uses a huge quantity of fertilizer every spring.
The museum owns a vast collection of medieval coins and seals.
The new reactor produces an enormous amount of heat during tests.
The village needed a large supply of timber for the bridge.
Our study found a tiny fraction of the samples were contaminated.
quiet: The ancient wall was decorated with carved figures of saints and kings.
Engineers built the tank from fairly cheap steel so it could hold rainwater.
These old batteries hold a charge poorly after a cold night.
The farm uses organic fertilizer every spring.
The museum owns a famous collection of medieval coins and seals.
The new reactor produces steady heat during tests.
The village needed seasoned timber for the bridge.
Our study found that some of the samples were contaminated.

notes: Card: no single token (' large' x3, ' big', ' little', ' a', ' moved'), Russian 'большую'. Probe: 'a large amount of water' reached 0.20, 'relatively big house' only 0.08. Low confidence best guess; near misses use non-size adjectives in the same slot.
